title: MCP Protocol Adoption in China: From Experimental to Production Infrastructure
summary: Analysis of the Chinese-language MCP ecosystem on GitHub reveals that MCP adoption has moved beyond experimental projects into production infrastructure. Chinese developers are building MCP servers for domestic services (WeChat, DingTalk, Feishu, Baidu, Alibaba Cloud), enterprise databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB), and internal tools. Major Chinese platforms — including Coze, Dify, JeecgBoot, and Trae — now include MCP support. Total Chinese-language MCP repositories with 300+ stars have grown to over 100, signaling mainstream adoption.
extractedSignals: MCP protocol has crossed the chasm in China's developer community — it is no longer an experimental standard but production infrastructure being integrated into major platforms and enterprise toolchains.

MCP's adoption in China follows a different pattern than in the West: rather than individual developers adding MCP to their personal coding agents, Chinese adoption is platform-driven — major low-code platforms, enterprise frameworks, and domestic AI coding tools are building MCP support directly into their products. This platform-driven adoption could accelerate MCP's network effects faster than the Western bottoms-up approach.
MCP has moved from experimental to production in the Chinese developer ecosystem.
Chinese MCP adoption is platform-driven: Coze, Dify, JeecgBoot, Trae all support MCP natively.
Chinese developers are building MCP servers for domestic services that don't exist in Western MCP registries.
